messages:
sasha (oncall): Incident bot fired: GPU pool saturation alarm in us-west-2. Queues climbing, ~20% throttled requests. paging @sasha :rotating_light:
incident-bot: SEV2 triggered - gpu_pool_utilization > 92% for 5m. Alerting oncall.
marco: I’m seeing queue_len=1200 on sharded router metrics, avg latency spiked to 1.8s. Affected model: rwf-13b-1q in dedicated pool.
devon: Confirmed. Autoscaler didn’t add capacity — it attempted scale but hit scale-limit=6 for the pool. Logs: `autoscaler:scale_request denied limit_reached`.
sasha (oncall): Is this after the batch/kv rollout earlier today?
ira: Yes — we rolled continuous-batching v2 with new `batch_window_ms=35` + kv-prefix-cache TTL reduction at 02:10 UTC. Canary looked fine.
marco: I’m seeing a sharp drop in batch hit ratio after the rollout: prefix_hits dropped from 88% -> 42% and effective tokens/sec fell ~30%. That explains node starvation.
lucy: Customer impact: a handful of high-traffic customers in us-west experienced increased 429s and timeouts. Support ticket spike incoming.
sasha (oncall): Immediate mitigation plan: 1) pause the autoscaler dry-run -> force scale to +2 nodes; 2) roll back batching/kv change; 3) add temporary traffic shaping for heavy routes. I’ll coordinate.
ops-bot: Running command: `./infractl pools scale --pool rwf-13b-1q --replicas 8 --reason "incident 2335012345"`
marco: Executed. New nodes provisioning. Watch for handshake/backpressure errors while shards rebalance.
devon: Meanwhile, reverting the config change. Reverting commit `a7f3d1e` that set `batch_window_ms` and `kv_prefix_ttl`.
incident-bot: Deploy rollback started for rwf-continuous-batching config.
ira: Rolling back TTL to 60s and batch_window_ms to 50ms. Patch applied to config service.
sasha (oncall): Can someone start a targeted canary to validate prefix hits? `curl -s http://metrics/api/query?query=batch_prefix_hit_ratio&region=us-west-2`
nate: Ran quick check: before rollback: {"prefix_hit_ratio": "0.42"}, after config rollback applied it climbed to 0.79 within 4 minutes. queue_len trending down to ~350.\ucode-block: "```\n[2026-03-15T02:45:12Z] router-1 queue_len=348 in_flight=412 throttle=0.12\n[2026-03-15T02:46:01Z] autoscaler scale_event: added 2 replicas -> total=8 status=online\n[2026-03-15T02:47:40Z] batchcache: prefix_hits=0.79 kv_evictions=12\n```"
sasha (oncall): Good. Keep autoscaler at +2 until we verify steady-state for 30m. Notify customers in impacted cohort and mark incident in status page as "degraded performance (partial)".
lucy: I posted an interim customer note in #support: "Experiencing elevated latencies and throttling for some workloads in us-west-2. Mitigation in progress."
marco: Suggest we also add a temporary override to autoscaler to ignore scale-limit for critical pools until rollout is re-validated. Today the soft hard-limit prevented recovery.
devon: Agreed. I've opened an infra PR to add `emergency_scale_override` gated by a feature-flag and audit-log.
sasha (oncall): Oncall handoff: @sasha -> @ira in 40m. Ira, if anything regresses, page the oncall channel immediately.
ira: I’m watching dashboards. I’ll take over at handoff. Please add postmortem owners.
sasha (oncall): Postmortem owners: marco (root cause), devon (autoscaler), lucy (customer comms). I'll file the incident ticket and set severity to SEV2 for now; upgrade if error rates spike again.
incident-bot: Incident 2335012345 marked acknowledged by sasha.
marco: Follow-ups: - run replay on canary prompt set to ensure quality not regressed by rollback - add unit test for prefix-cache keying that broke after config change - instrument autoscaler with clearer reason codes (limit vs capacity)
sasha (oncall): Thanks all. We’ll reconvene in 30m for an update and decision on scaling back the manual replicas. :thumbsup:
